ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r1.claim: Libadan is the plural of libdah, meaning intertwined or multilayered; it depicts tawḥīd as alien in the very house built for worship of the one God, where opponents crowd the Prophet during prayer and preaching to harass him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r1.anchor: which means something which is intertwined or something which is multi-layered.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh refers to the Prophet; the affectionate expression also presents invoking God alone as a servant’s most natural and logical course, though some consciences recoil from it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p519/r2.anchor: refers to the Prophet (sws). The expression reflects affection

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r6.speaker: الجمهور وابن هرمز وطلحة ونافع وأبو بكر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r6.claim: The majority open the hamza of وأنه لما قام; Ibn Hurmuz, Talha, Nafi, and Abu Bakr read it with kasra as an independent clause. Abdullah is Muhammad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وأنه لما قام عبد الله بفتح الهمزة، عطفا على قراءتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r7.claim: They take كادوا to mean the jinn nearly crowded around Muhammad to hear the Quran; Hasan and Qatada instead identify Quraysh and Arabs gathering against him, while Ibn Jubayr takes it as the jinn addressing their people about his followers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس والضحاك: ينقضون عليه لاستماع القرآن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r8.claim: He explains عبد الله as humble self-reference in the Prophet's account, or as stressing that worshiping God is neither strange nor objectionable; the prayer was at dawn in Nakhlah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p300/r8.anchor: ومعنى قام يدعوه: قام يعبده، يريد قيامه لصلاة الفجر بنخلة حين أتاه الجن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r1.claim: He says the jinn crowded around in amazement at the Prophet's worship, imitating the companions and admiring the unfamiliar Quran; Abu Hayyan says this embellishes an earlier view rhetorically.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r1.anchor: أي يزدحمون عليه متراكمين، تعجبا مما رأوا من عبادته، واقتداء أصحابه به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r2.speaker: الجمهور وابن عباس ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r2.claim: The majority read لِبَدا as groups piled over one another; Ibn Abbas glosses it as helpers, while other readers vary its vowels and derive it from related collective forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: لبدا بكسر اللام وفتح الباء جمع لبدة، نحو: كسرة وكسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r3.claim: They say humans and jinn massed against the Prophet's call to extinguish it, but God would uphold and complete His light.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r3.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد: لما قام الرسول للدعوة، تلبدت الإنس والجن على هذا الأمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r4.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r4.claim: He offers the remote view that Abdullah is Noah, whose people nearly killed him; identifying him as Abdullah ibn Salam is even more far-fetched.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p301/r4.anchor: وأبعد من قال عبد الله هنا نوح عليه السلام، كاد قومه يقتلونه حتى استنقذه الله منهم

FARRA:v3p194/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p194/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p194/r1.claim: The reading lubadan describes the men, like plural adjectives meaning bowing, kneeling, and prostrating.
FARRA:v3p194/r1.anchor: ومن قرأ: «لبدا» فإنه أراد أن يجعلها من صفة الرجال،

NAHHAS:v5p52/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p52/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p52/r1.claim: An unattributed poem describes a well-armed lion with a mane and untrimmed claws; the excerpt does not identify its lexical target.
NAHHAS:v5p52/r1.anchor: ( لدى أسد شاكي السلاح مقاذف … له لبد أظفاره لم تقلم )

BIQAI-FULL:v8p194/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p194/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p194/r1.claim: It is unsurprising when a servant calls upon and devotes himself to his own Master; the real cause for amazement is worshipping another or inclining even slightly toward another.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p194/r1.anchor: إنما يعجب ممن دعا غير سيده أو مال إليه أدنى ميل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p194/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p194/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p194/r2.claim: The opening may mean God revealed that when Muhammad stood in prayer the jinn nearly crowded over him, or may be the jinn recounting to their people what they saw of his prayer and his companions' gathering around him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p194/r2.anchor: أوحي إلي أو قال الجن لمن أطاعهم من قومهم حاكين ما رأوا من صلاته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p194/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p194/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p194/r3.claim: Calling Muhammad God's servant highlights that he worships the supreme King; even a servant of the least master would not be treated this way, much less the King of kings.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p194/r3.anchor: فكيف إذا كان سيده مالك الملك وملك الملوك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r1.claim: The apparent setting is Muhammad praying in the valley of Nakhlah, where jinn sent toward Tihamah by Iblis saw him, crowded close, heard the Quran and his monotheism, and believed.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r1.anchor: لما قمت في الصلاة أعبد الله في بطن نخلة ورآني الجن الذي وجههم إبليس نحو تهامة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Saʿid ibn Jubayr are also reported to interpret the passage as the jinn telling their people about the Prophet's prayer and the companions standing closely around him to pray and learn.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r2.anchor: ويحكى هذا القول عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وسعيد بن جبير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r3.claim: An envoy sent by the Persian king described Muslims praying in orderly rows behind one leader, all bowing, prostrating, sitting, and acting together; the king was struck by this and mentioned Umar.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r3.anchor: إذا صلوا صفوا أنفسهم صفوفا ويقدمهم رجل يقومون بقيامة ويسجدون بسجوده

BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r4.speaker: مكحول
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r4.claim: Makhul, as quoted by Abu Hayyan, says seventy thousand followed the Prophet on the night of the jinn and dispersed at daybreak.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p195/r4.anchor: ونقل أبو حيان عن مكحول أنه بلغ من تابع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة الجن سبعين ألفا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r1.claim: It is strained to identify the servant in this sequence as Noah; Ibn Jubayr instead reads the statement as jinn reporting to their people about Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r1.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: معنى الآية، إنما قول الجن لقومهم يحكون، والعبد محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r2.claim: The pronoun in كادوا refers to the Prophet's companions who follow and emulate him in prayer; they formed a crowd on him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r2.anchor: والضمير في كادوا لأصحابه الذين يطوعون له ويقتدون به في الصلاة، فهم عليه لبد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r3.claim: لبد describes crowds piled over one another, as in the poet's image of locusts covering something.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r3.anchor: واللبد الجماعات شبهت بالشيء المتلبد بعضه فوق بعض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r4.speaker: عبد بن مناف بن ربع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r4.claim: The poet's line depicts a dense covering like a swarm of locusts, called جاني because it gathers what it eats, with جابي also transmitted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r4.anchor: يريد الجراد سماه جانيا لأنه يجني كل شيء، ويروى جابيا بالباء لأنه يجبي الأشياء بأكله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses لبد as helpers; several readers also vary its vowel pattern.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r5.anchor: وقرأ جمهور السبعة وابن عباس: «لبدا» بكسر اللام جمع لبدة، وقال ابن عباس: أعوانا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r6.claim: If the pronoun refers to the jinn, they crowded around Muhammad to listen to the remembrance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p384/r6.anchor: فإن قدرنا الضمير للجن فتقصفهم عليه لاستماع الذكر، وهذا تأويل الحسن وقتادة

JISHUMI:v10p7124/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r1.claim: Uprightness may bring the reward of Paradise and may be a cause of expanded provision.
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r1.anchor: أن الجنة تنال بالاستقامة، وأنها يجوز أن تكون سببا لسعة الرزق

JISHUMI:v10p7124/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r2.claim: The passage requires reflection on proofs.
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r2.anchor: ومنها: على وجوب التفكر في الأدلة

JISHUMI:v10p7124/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r5.claim: The phrase about people nearly becoming a compact crowd around the Prophet could be praise or blame.
JISHUMI:v10p7124/r5.anchor: ويحتمل قوله: (كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا) أن يكون مدحا وذما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r1.claim: عبد الله means the Prophet. The wording reflects the Prophet speaking of himself with humility, or stresses that God's servant worshipping Him is rational and unsurprising.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r1.anchor: { عبد الله } النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم . فإن قلت : هلا قيل : رسول الله أو النبي ؟

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r2.claim: قام يدعوه means he rose to worship, specifically for dawn prayer at Nakhlah when jinn came and listened to his recitation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r2.anchor: ( قام يدعوه ) قام يعبده ، يريد : قيامه لصلاة الفجر بنخلة حين أتاه الجن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r3.claim: One interpretation says the jinn crowded around Muhammad in wonder at his worship, the companions' example, and the extraordinary Qur'an they heard.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r3.anchor: { كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا } أي يزدحمون عليه متراكمين تعجبا مما رأوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r4.claim: Alternatively, the polytheists nearly swarmed against him in united opposition when he preached worship of God alone.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r4.anchor: وقيل معناه : لما قام رسولا يعبد الله وحده مخالفا للمشركين في عبادتهم الآلهة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r5.claim: لبدا is a heap, with readings لبدا, لبدا, and لبدا representing the collective pile or plural forms like ساجد/سجد and صبور/صبر.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r5.anchor: { لبدا } جمع لبدة وهو ما تلبد بعضه على بعض ، ومنها ( لبدة الأسد )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r6.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r6.claim: Qatada says humans and jinn gathered against the Prophet to extinguish his mission, but God chose to support and make him prevail.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r6.anchor: وعن قتادة : تلبدت الإنس والجن على هذا الأمر ليطفئوه فأبى الله إلا أن ينصره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r7.claim: With kasra on وإنه, the words become the jinn's report to their people about what they saw of the Prophet's prayer and his companions crowding to follow him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p632/r7.anchor: ومن قرأ ( وإنه ) بالكسر : جعله من كلام الجن : قالوه لقومهم حين رجعوا إليهم

MUQATIL:72:15-23/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:72:15-23/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:72:15-23/r5.claim: The account returns to the nine jinn: when the Prophet worshipped at Nakhlah between Mecca and Taif, they nearly crowded over him, eager and amazed to hear the Quran.
MUQATIL:72:15-23/r5.anchor: { وأنه لما قام عبد الله } النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم { يدعوه } يعني يعبده في بطن نخلة بين مكة والطائف

TABATABAI:72:20-23/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r1.claim: One view takes both pronouns as referring to the jinn, who crowded around the Prophet in amazement at his worship and recitation.
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r1.anchor: وقيل الضميران للجن وإنهم اجتمعوا عليه وتراكموا ينظرون إليه متعجبين

TABATABAI:72:20-23/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r2.claim: Another view takes both pronouns as the believers gathered around the Prophet to follow his prayer and listen to the Quran.
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r2.anchor: وقيل الضميران للمؤمنين بالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم المجتمعين عليه اقتداء به في صلاته

TABATABAI:72:20-23/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r3.claim: The following verses do not fit either proposed referent as well as the author's earlier contextual reading.
TABATABAI:72:20-23/r3.anchor: والوجهان لا يلائمان سياق الآيات التالية تلك الملاءمة

THALABI:v10p54/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p54/r10.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v10p54/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says the jinn nearly crowded onto one another, eager to hear the Qur'an when Muhammad called on God, proclaimed His oneness, and recited.
THALABI:v10p54/r10.anchor: كادوا يعني: الجن يكونون عليه لبدا أي يركبون بعضهم بعضا، ويزدحمون ويسقطون حرصا منهم على استماع القرآن

THALABI:v10p54/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p54/r11.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p54/r11.claim: A report through Atiyya from Ibn Abbas gives the same explanation of the jinn crowding around the Prophet to listen.

THALABI:v10p55/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p55/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p55/r1.claim: On return to their people, the jinn recounted the Companions' obedience and devotion to the Prophet, including following him in prayer.
THALABI:v10p55/r1.anchor: هذا من قول النفر من الجن لما رجعوا إلى قومهم أخبروهم بما رأوا من طاعة أصحاب رسول الله

THALABI:v10p55/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p55/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد
THALABI:v10p55/r2.claim: They say jinn and humans massed against Muhammad to extinguish God's light, but God completed His cause and supported him against opponents.
THALABI:v10p55/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد: يعني لما قام عبد الله بالدعوة تلبدت الجن والإنس

THALABI:v10p55/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p55/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p55/r3.claim: Libad means groups piled on one another; the word also names a large swarm of locusts, matted hair, and a lion's mane.
THALABI:v10p55/r3.anchor: وأصل اللبد: الجماعات بعضها فوق بعض

THALABI:v10p55/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p55/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p55/r4.claim: Zuhayr's line illustrates libad as a lion's mane.
THALABI:v10p55/r4.anchor: لدى أسد شاك السلاح خبان … له لبد أظفاره لم تقلم

THALABI:v10p55/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p55/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p55/r5.claim: The common reading has kasra on lām and fatḥa on bā; Abu Ubayda and Abu Hatim prefer it, with singular lubda in kasra.
THALABI:v10p55/r5.anchor: قراءة العامة واختيار أبي عبيدة وأبي حاتم

THALABI:v10p55/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p55/r6.speaker: مجاهد وابن محيصن
THALABI:v10p55/r6.claim: They read with ḍamma on lām and fatḥa on bā, with singular lubda in ḍamma.
THALABI:v10p55/r6.anchor: ولبد بضم اللام وفتح الباء وهي قراءة مجاهد وابن محيص وواحدتها لبدة بضم اللام

THALABI:v10p55/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p55/r7.speaker: أبو حيوة
THALABI:v10p55/r7.claim: Abu Haywa reads with ḍamma on both lām and bā, and gives lubayd as the singular.
THALABI:v10p55/r7.anchor: ولبد بضم اللام والباء وهي قراءة أبي حيوة واحدتها لبيد

THALABI:v10p55/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p55/r8.speaker: الحسن وأبو جعفر
THALABI:v10p55/r8.claim: Hasan and Abu Jaafar read with a doubled bā, likening the plural form to other doubled plurals such as rukkaʿ and sujjad.
THALABI:v10p55/r8.anchor: ولبد بضم اللام وتشديد الباء وهي قراءة الحسن وأبي جعفر وواحدها لابد مثل راكع ركع وساجد وسجد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p49/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p49/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p49/r8.claim: Muhammad uniquely attained complete servanthood, detached from states that diminish it, and God describes him as His servant at the beginning of the journey and in another verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p49/r8.anchor: فكان عبدا محضا زاهدا في جميع الأحوال التي تخرجه عن مرتبة العبودية

ELMALILI:72:1-19/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19/r15.claim: The clauses in verses 5, 7, and 19 admit either of the two syntactic readings.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r20.claim: The phrase wa annahu is kasra for Nafiʿ and Abu Bakr from Asim, but fatḥ for Hafs and the other readings.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r20.anchor: Burada أَنَّهُ Nâfi‘ve Âsım’dan Ebû Bekir kıraatlerinde kesr ile, Hafs’ta vesâir kıraatlerin hepsinde feth ile okunur.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r21.claim: Some connect the kasra reading to the jinns’ speech, but Elmalılı finds a divine resumptive clause more fitting because the intervening verse makes the connection less elegant.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r21.anchor: kesr kıraatinde vâv atıf olmayıp taraf-ı ilâhîden istînaf olması daha muvâfık olur.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r22.claim: The fatḥ reading attaches the clause to the revelation; on these readings, the subject of kādū may be the jinn or both jinn and humans.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r22.anchor: Feth[^37] ile okunması ise vahiy cümlesine atıftır. Bu suretlerde كَادُوا۟ zamiri cine veya cin ve inse ait olur.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r23.claim: Abdullah means God’s servant, Muhammad; this title signals humility alongside his special devotion in fulfilling servitude to God.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r23.anchor: “Abdullah” Allah’ın kulu, bu vahiy kendisine indirilmiş olan Hazret-i Peygamber’in kendisidir.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r24.claim: On one reading, the listening jinn crowded densely around the Prophet, almost piling together like felt, because his worship and prayer were unfamiliar to them.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r24.anchor: o dinleyen cinler ta‘cillerinden kesret ve izdiham ile etrafına öyle toplandılar ki az daha keçe gibi birbirlerine geçeceklerdi

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r25.claim: If the passage is the jinns’ speech, it means hostile polytheists crowded around the Prophet while he prayed, nearly pressing together.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r25.anchor: Cinler kavimlerine şunu da söylediler: “O Allah’ın kulu kalkmış Allah’a dua ederken müşrik insanlar ona adâvetle aleyhine öyle toplanmışlardı

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r26.speaker: قتادة
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r26.claim: Qatada’s third interpretation is that unbelieving jinn and humans gathered against the Prophet to thwart his mission; God protects and grants him victory, and the view fits both readings and 72:13.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r26.anchor: Katâde’den mervî olan üçüncü bir mâna daha vardır. Şöyle ki: İns ü cin kâfirleri onun işini, kıyam ve davetini ibtal etmek için aleyhinde öyle toplanmışlardı

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r27.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r27.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r27.claim: Either way, the passage informs the Prophet of outward and inward events and feelings occurring beyond his presence.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r27.anchor: Ve her iki takdirde de Peygamber’e gıyâbında cereyan eden zâhirî ve bâtınî ahvâl ve hissiyâtı ihbardır.

ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r28.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r28.speaker: author
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r28.claim: Elmalılı says the commands that follow fit the flow of these verses well.
ELMALILI:72:1-19#4/r28.anchor: Bundan sonraki emirler, âyetlerin sevkiyle de gayet mütenâsibdir.

FARRA:v3p193/r14.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p193/r14.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p193/r14.claim: The servant is the Prophet, when the jinn came to him at Batn Nakhla one night.
FARRA:v3p193/r14.anchor: يريد: النبي صلى الله عليه ليلة أتاه الجن ببطن نخلة

FARRA:v3p193/r15.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p193/r15.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p193/r15.claim: The jinn nearly formed a dense crowd around the Prophet, eager for and desiring the Qur’an.
FARRA:v3p193/r15.anchor: كادوا يركبون النبي صلى الله عليه رغبة في القرآن، وشهوة له

FARRA:v3p193/r16.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p193/r16.speaker: بعضهم
FARRA:v3p193/r16.claim: Some readers recite «لبدا»; al-Farrāʾ considers both readings equivalent, noting the Arabic forms «لبدة» and «لبدة».
FARRA:v3p193/r16.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم : «لبدا » والمعنى فيهما- والله أعلم- واحد، يقال: لبدة، ولبدة

JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r5.speaker: هشام بن عمار عن ابن عامر
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r5.claim: In Hishām ibn ʿAmmār’s transmission, Ibn ʿĀmir reads lubadan with ḍamma on the lām; the rest read it with kasra.
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر في رواية هشام بن عمار: لبدا بضم اللام، الباقون بكسرها

JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r6.claim: Both vowelings of libda/lubda mean accumulated, thickly packed.
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r6.anchor: واللبدة واللبدة بضم اللام وكسرها بمعنى واحد

JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد، ابن محيصن
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid and Ibn Muḥayṣin are also reported to read the word with ḍamma on the lām, like Ibn ʿĀmir.
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r7.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد وابن محيصن مثل قراءة ابن عامر

JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r8.claim: Four dialects are listed: lubad with kasra on lām and fatḥ on bāʾ, lubad with ḍamma on lām and fatḥ on bāʾ, lubud with both letters rounded, and lubbad with a doubled bāʾ; the latter forms are attributed to Abū Ḥaywa, al-Ḥasan, and al-Jaḥdarī respectively.
JISHUMI:v10p7119#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: فيه أربع لغات: لبد بكسر اللام وفتح الباء، وعليه - أكثر القراء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r8.claim: The servant of God who stood at Batn Nakhlah to pray was the Prophet Muhammad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r8.anchor: وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه } أي: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما قام ببطن نخلة يدعو الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r9.claim: The jinn nearly climbed over one another, crowding eagerly to hear the recitation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:72:16-19/r9.anchor: كادوا يكونون عليه } كاد الجن يتراكبون ويزدحمون حرصا على ما يسمعون، ورغبة فيه.

RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p136/r7.claim: One reading pattern gives fatḥ to clauses that belong to revelation and kasr to the jinn’s speech; the final clauses about mosques and the Prophet’s standing are exceptions to the jinn’s speech.

RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r1.claim: All agree that “the servant of God” means the Prophet Muḥammad.
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أن عبدالله هو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قول الجميع

RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r2.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r2.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says this clause is the jinn’s speech rather than revelation, since the Messenger would not naturally speak about himself in the third person; Rāzī says this is possible and compares 19:85.
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r2.anchor: قال الواحدي : إن هذا من كلام الجن لا من جملة الموحى

RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r3.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r3.claim: Most interpreters treat the clause as part of the revelation; otherwise non-jinn speech would interrupt the jinn’s words and damage the composition.
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r3.anchor: والأكثرون على أنه من جملة الموحى

RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r4.claim: The grammatical choice tracks the interpretation: the initial hamza is open if the clause is revelation and kasr if it is the jinn’s speech.
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r4.anchor: أن من جعله من جملة الموحى فتح الهمزة في أن

RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r5.claim: If this is revelation and “they” means the jinn, the Prophet stood worshipping at dawn when they arrived; they nearly crowded over one another around him, amazed by his worship and the Qurʾān.
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r5.anchor: أحدها : إلى الجن ، ومعنى { قام يدعوه }

RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r6.claim: Another reading makes “they” the polytheists, who nearly crowded around the Prophet because he worshipped one God instead of their idols and they combined against him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r6.anchor: والثاني : لما قدم رسول الله يعبد الله وحده

RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r7.claim: Qatāda says humans and jinn massed together against the Prophet to defeat the truth and extinguish God’s light, but God resolved to support and exalt him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r7.anchor: وهو قول قتادة : لما قام عبدالله تلبدت

RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r8.claim: If the clause is the jinn’s speech, the first two explanations of who nearly crowded around the Prophet can also apply.
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r8.anchor: وأما على قول من قال : إنه من كلام الجن

RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r9.claim: Libadan is the plural of libda, something matted and piled on itself; the same root describes tightly stuck material, rugs, and the matted mane behind a lion’s shoulders.
RAZI-FULL:v30p144#2/r9.anchor: فهو جمع لبدة وهو ما تلبد بعضه على بعض

RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r1.speaker: قُرِىء
RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r1.claim: The word is read with ḍamma on lām as lubada, equivalent in meaning to libda; other readings treat it as the plural of lābid or of lubūd.
RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r1.anchor: وقرىء : { لبدا } بضم اللام واللبدة في معنى اللبدة

RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r2.speaker: قُرِىء
RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r2.claim: A further reading has ḍamma on both lām and bāʾ and treats lubada as the plural of lubūd, like ṣubar as the plural of ṣabūr.
RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r2.anchor: وقرىء أيضا : { لبدا } بضم اللام والباء جمع لبود كصبر جمع صبور

RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r3.speaker: زهير
RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r3.claim: Zuhayr’s line describes a lion with a mane whose claws have not been trimmed, using libd for the matted mane.

RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r4.claim: Calling himself “the servant of God” suits the Prophet’s humility if the words are revelation; if they are the jinn’s, the point is that disbelievers tried to stop someone worshipping God, which accords with reason.
RAZI-FULL:v30p145/r4.anchor: لأنه إن كان هذا الكلام من جملة الموحى

STUDYQURAN:72:19/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r1.claim: ʿAbd Allāh is one of the Quran’s seven names for the Prophet and a very common name for him in Islamic tradition.
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r1.anchor: is one of the seven names by which the Prophet is called in the Quran

STUDYQURAN:72:19/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r2.claim: Servanthood to God is a highest spiritual station because it expresses complete surrender to God.
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r2.anchor: To be the servant of God is one of the highest spiritual stations, as it represents complete surrender to God

STUDYQURAN:72:19/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r3.speaker: Bg, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r3.claim: The jinn were amazed by the Quran and nearly piled on one another to hear it.
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r3.anchor: the jinn, who were amazed at the Quran and nearly piled upon one another to hear it

STUDYQURAN:72:19/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r4.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r4.claim: Alternatively, the jinn told their companions how amazed they were by the Prophet’s Companions’ devotion.
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r4.anchor: the jinn reporting to their own companions how amazed they were to see the devotion of the Prophet’s Companions

STUDYQURAN:72:19/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r5.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r5.claim: The swarm may mean Quraysh disbelievers and jinn obstructed the Prophet and pressed around him as he prayed at the Kaʿbah.
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r5.anchor: the disbelievers among the Quraysh and among the jinn who would put obstacles in the Prophet’s way and press in upon him

STUDYQURAN:72:19/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r6.claim: The preceding verses favor the jinn interpretation, while following verses favor Quraysh disbelievers.
STUDYQURAN:72:19/r6.anchor: The verses before this verse support the interpretation of it as a reference to the jinn, while those after it support its interpretation

TAB-FULL:v23p342/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r1.claim: Libda is the singular of libad; Al-Ṭabarī gives plural forms from both kasra and ḍamma patterns, including lābid and lubad.
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r1.anchor: اللام لبدة، ومن كسرها جمعها لبد؛ وضم اللام لبدة، ومن ضمها جمعها لبد بضم اللام

TAB-FULL:v23p342/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r2.speaker: قراء الأمصار وابن محيصن
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r2.claim: City readers use kasra in libad, while Ibn Muḥayṣin uses ḍamma; both mean the same, and Al-Ṭabarī prefers the city readers’ reading.
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r2.anchor: وقراء الأمصار على كسر اللام من لبد، غير ابن محيصن فإنه كان يضمها، وهما بمعنى واحد؛

TAB-FULL:v23p342/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r3.claim: Arabs call a dense pile of locusts libda; ʿAbd Manāf ibn Ribʿī al-Hudhalī uses jābiyan libadan for locusts, with jābiya describing locusts that consume everything.
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r3.anchor: ومنه قول عبد مناف بن ربعي الهذلي: [البحر البسيط] صابوا بستة أبيات وأربعة … حتى كأن عليهم جابيا لبدا

TAB-FULL:v23p342/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the jinn heard the Prophet reciting the Qurʾān and drew near without his noticing until the Messenger came and taught him the revelation.
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} [الجن: 19] يقول: لما سمعوا النبي

TAB-FULL:v23p342/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the jinn nearly climbed onto the Prophet out of eagerness for what they heard of the Qurʾān.
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r5.anchor: قال: سمعت أبا معاذ، يقول: ثنا عبيد، قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} [الجن: 19] كادوا يركبونه حرصا

TAB-FULL:v23p342/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r6.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r6.claim: On the interpretation that the jinn crowded around after hearing the Qurʾān, this clause is treated as part of what was revealed to the Prophet, continuing the report introduced at 72:1.
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r6.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: ومن قال هذا القول جعل قوله

TAB-FULL:v23p342/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r7.claim: In another account, Ibn ʿAbbās says the jinn described seeing the Prophet pray while his Companions followed his bowing and prostration, marveling at their obedience.
TAB-FULL:v23p342/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: قول الجن لقومهم: {لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} [الجن: 19] قال: لما رأوه يصلي وأصحابه

TAB-FULL:v23p344/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the Prophet’s Companions followed him, bowing when he bowed and prostrating when he prostrated.
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في قوله: {وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} [الجن: 19] قال: كان أصحاب نبي الله

TAB-FULL:v23p344/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r2.speaker: أصحاب قول ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r2.claim: For the report that the jinn spoke of the Companions’ obedience, the opening hamza may be read open and coordinated with 72:3, or read with kasra as a new start.
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس وسعيد فتح الألف من قوله

TAB-FULL:v23p344/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r3.claim: Another view takes this as God’s report to the Prophet that humans and jinn joined together against him to extinguish the truth, but God completed and vindicated it.
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل ذلك من خبر الله الذي أوحاه إلى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم لعلمه أن الإنس والجن تظاهروا عليه

TAB-FULL:v23p344/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r4.claim: Qatāda says humans and jinn massed against the Prophet to put out this light, but God insisted on supporting and making him prevail over opponents.
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} [الجن: 19] قال: تلبدت الإنس والجن على هذا الأمر ليطفئوه

TAB-FULL:v23p344/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says people joined forces against the Messenger.
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} [الجن: 19] قال: تظاهروا عليه بعضهم على بعض

TAB-FULL:v23p344/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r6.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r6.claim: Those who take the clause as God’s report of opposition read the opening hamza open.
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r6.anchor: ومن قال هذا القول فتح الألف من قوله: {وأنه} [الجن: 19]

TAB-FULL:v23p344/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the report that Arabs nearly united against Muhammad to extinguish God’s light: it follows God’s speech in 72:18 and after forbidding invocation it naturally reports opposition to that command, not respondents to invocation.
TAB-FULL:v23p344/r7.anchor: وأولى الأقوال بالصواب في ذلك قول من قال: ذلك خبر من الله

TAB-FULL:v23p347/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r1.claim: When Muhammad stood calling on God and proclaiming there is no god but God, the people nearly crowded over him in dense groups.
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه} [الجن: 19] قال: لما قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

TAB-FULL:v23p347/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r2.claim: Lubad means crowds piled over one another; its singular is lubda.
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r2.anchor: واللبد: الشيء الذي بعضه فوق بعض

TAB-FULL:v23p347/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the Messenger stood proclaiming God’s oneness and calling people to their Lord, and the Arabs nearly gathered against him altogether.
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r3.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه} [الجن: 19] قال: لما قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

TAB-FULL:v23p347/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explains that the people piled over the Prophet.
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في قوله: {كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} [الجن: 19] قال: تراكبوا عليه

TAB-FULL:v23p347/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r5.claim: In another report, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says they were one on top of another.
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} [الجن: 19] قال: بعضهم على بعض

TAB-FULL:v23p347/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the crowds as helpers.
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله {كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} [الجن: 19] يقول: أعوانا

TAB-FULL:v23p347/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r7.claim: Mujāhid says they were all together.
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} [الجن: 19] قال: جميعا

TAB-FULL:v23p347/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says they were all together.
TAB-FULL:v23p347/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد {كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} [الجن: 19] قال: جميعا

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r1.claim: The verses derive the Prophet’s mission, divine oneness, and resurrection from the jinn story, then close by indicating the messenger’s protection from error.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r1.anchor: في الآيات تسجيل للنبوة وذكر وحدانيته تعالى والمعاد كالاستنتاج من القصة وتختتم بالإشارة إلى عصمة الرسالة

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r12.claim: Libad is the plural of libda: accumulated, piled together.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r12.anchor: اللبد بالكسر فالفتح جمع لبدة بالضم فالسكون المجتمعة المتراكمة

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r13.claim: ʿAbd Allāh is the Prophet, as the next verse shows; calling him God’s servant prepares for ‘I invoke my Lord.’
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r13.anchor: والمراد بعبد الله النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كما تدل عليه الآية التالية

TABATABAI:72:18-20/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r14.claim: The plural pronouns most fittingly refer to polytheists who crowded around the Prophet as he prayed and recited, mocking and raising their voices above his.
TABATABAI:72:18-20/r14.anchor: والأنسب لسياق الآيات التالية أن يكون مرجع ضميري الجمع في قوله { كادوا يكونون } المشركين

BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r4.claim: This is another part of what was revealed: that the matter was so when God's servant stood.
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r4.anchor: من جملة الموحى به أي وأوحى إلى أن الشأن

BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r5.claim: Abd Allah refers to the Prophet, counted among his names because he is the true servant, joined to the Greatest Name distinctly while manifesting it comprehensively.
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r5.anchor: إلى النبي عليه السلام ولذا جعلوا في أسمائه لأنه هو العبد الحقيقي

BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r6.claim: Tradition says the Prophet liked no name more than Abd Allah; his perfect station in servitude could not be matched by others.
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r6.anchor: آن حضرت را عليه السلام هي نام ارين خوشتر نيامده ه شريطه عادت وعبوديت

BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r7.claim: The Quran calls him God's servant in the Night Journey and in the revelation of the Criterion, linking the name to his ascent and receiving revelation.
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r7.anchor: تبارك الذي نزل الفرقان على عبده

BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r8.speaker: شاعر
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r8.claim: The cited Persian couplet praises God's servant as marked by beloved servitude, whose path through bondage is unknown to kings.
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r8.anchor: آن بنده شعار بندكى دوست كزجمله بندكان كزين اوست داند ببند كيش راهى

BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r9.claim: Calling him the servant highlights the cause of his standing and worship—his servanthood—and expresses humility, as though he said, God revealed that when I stood.
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r9.anchor: وإيراده عليه السلام بلفظ العبد للإشعار بما هو المقتضي لقيامه وعبادته وهو العبودية

BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r10.claim: On the accusative reading, the clause can be understood as the Prophet speaking of himself; on Nafi and Abu Bakr's reading, Abd Allah must signal the cause of his standing.
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r10.anchor: وهذا على قراءة الفتح وإما على قراءة نافع وأبي بكر فيتعين كونه للإشعار بالمقتضى

BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r11.claim: The phrase is circumstantial of the one who stood: he was worshipping God, in the Fajr prayer at Nakhlah described earlier.
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r11.anchor: حال من فاعل قام أي يعبده وذلك قيامه لصلاة الفجر بنخلة

BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r12.claim: On the accusative reading, كادوا refers to the jinn, who crowded over Muhammad in amazement at his worship and Quran and imitated his companions' prayer postures.
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r12.anchor: أي قرب الجن {يكونون عليه لبدا} جمع لبدة

BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r13.claim: Libad is the plural of libda: things piled and stuck together, like a lion's mane; here it describes a dense crowd.
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r13.anchor: وهي ما تلبد بعضه على بعض أي تراكب وتلاصق

BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r14.claim: On the genitive reading, if the phrase is the jinn's speech, كادوا instead refers to Muhammad's companions following him in prayer.
BURSEVI:v10p152#2/r14.anchor: وعلى قراءة الكسر إذا جعل مقول الجن فضمير كادوا لأصحابه عليه السلام الذين كانوا مقتدين به في الصلاة

BURSEVI:v10p153/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p153/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v10p153/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās’s account places only seven or nine jinn at Nakhlah, so crowding in the open space by the reciter makes little sense.
BURSEVI:v10p153/r1.anchor: ما ذهب إليه ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما على ما ذهب إليه المفسرون فلا معنى للازدحام إذ كان الجن بنخلة نفرا سبعة أو تسعة

BURSEVI:v10p153/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p153/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p153/r2.claim: They may have approached from one direction until nearly piling up; alternatively, nafar may be figurative, though that makes specifying their number pointless.
BURSEVI:v10p153/r2.anchor: حتى كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا أو بأن يتجوز في النفر

BURSEVI:v10p153/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p153/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURSEVI:v10p153/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd places the crowd at al-Ḥajūn after returning from Nakhlah; Bursevī objects that this was witnessed, not revealed, and that few companions were with the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v10p153/r3.anchor: بطريق المشاهدة على ما أسفلناه في الأحقاف

BURSEVI:v10p153/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p153/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p153/r4.claim: According to Insān al-ʿuyūn, only Zayd ibn Ḥārithah was with the Prophet, further undermining the crowding account.
BURSEVI:v10p153/r4.anchor: بل لم يكن إلا زيد ابن حارثة رضي الله عنه

TABRISI:72:1/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1/r4.speaker: نافع وعاصم برواية أبي بكر
TABRISI:72:1/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim in Abu Bakr’s transmission read wa-annahu lammā qāma with kasr; the other readers use fatḥ.
TABRISI:72:1/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم برواية أبي بكر وأنه لما قام بالكسر والباقون بالفتح

TABRISI:72:1#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1#2/r7.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:72:1#2/r7.claim: Sibawayh connects wa-annahu lammā qāma to revelation; the clause can be cut off and begun independently, as with al-masājid.
TABRISI:72:1#2/r7.anchor: فإنه على { أوحي إلي } ويكون أن يقطع من قوله { أوحي }

TABRISI:72:1#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:72:1#2/r8.claim: With fatḥ, the clause may be attached to revelation, though another independent parse is possible.
TABRISI:72:1#2/r8.anchor: ومن قرأ كل ذلك بالفتح فإنه للحمل على أوحي ويجوز أن يكون على غيره

TABRISI:72:1#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1#2/r9.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:72:1#2/r9.claim: After quoted speech and a conditional faʾ, the following clause can begin independently with an omitted introduction; Sibawayh applies this to examples including 72:23.
TABRISI:72:1#2/r9.anchor: وكذلك ما بعد فاء الجزاء لأن ما بعد فاء الجزاء موضع ابتداء

TABRISI:72:19-20/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:19-20/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:72:19-20/r1.claim: “The servant of God” refers to Muhammad.

TABRISI:72:19-20/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:19-20/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:72:19-20/r2.claim: Muhammad was calling people with “There is no god but God,” inviting them to it, and reciting the Qur’an.
TABRISI:72:19-20/r2.anchor: بقول لا إله إلا الله ويدعو إليه ويقرأ القرآن

TABRISI:72:19-20/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:19-20/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
TABRISI:72:19-20/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the jinn nearly piled on one another around Muhammad, eager to hear the Qur’an.

TABRISI:72:19-20/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:19-20/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:72:19-20/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the jinn told their people that the Prophet’s companions crowded around him to hear the Qur’an, each wanting to be closest.
TABRISI:72:19-20/r4.anchor: فيتلبد بعضهم على بعض عن سعيد بن جبير.

TABRISI:72:19-20/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:19-20/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:72:19-20/r5.claim: Another view treats the clause as part of what God revealed about the jinn’s eagerness to listen.
TABRISI:72:19-20/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو من جملة ما أوحى الله إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:72:19-20/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:19-20/r6.speaker: قتادة والحسن
TABRISI:72:19-20/r6.claim: Qatada and al-Hasan say Quraysh crowded around Muhammad to overwhelm him and stop his call to monotheism, but God gave him victory.
TABRISI:72:19-20/r6.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن وعلى هذا فيكون ابتداء كلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r1.claim: The conjunction can be read with fatḥa, linked to “it was revealed,” or with kasra as a new sentence.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r2.speaker: الجميع
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r2.claim: Everyone identifies “the servant of God” as the Prophet; they said this as he prayed in the valley of Mecca and recited the Quran.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r2.anchor: وقوله: {عبد الله} يعني النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- في قول الجميع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r4.claim: They nearly piled on the Prophet out of eagerness for and love of the Quran, as al-Kalbi and Muqatil report.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r4.anchor: واختار الفراء: كادوا يركبون النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- رغبة في القرآن وشهوة له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r5.claim: Al-Farra selects the reading that they nearly climbed upon the Prophet out of desire and longing for the Quran.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r5.anchor: واختار الفراء: كادوا يركبون النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- رغبة في القرآن وشهوة له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the jinn who heard the Quran and marveled at it nearly fell upon the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج: كادوا الجن الذين سمعوا القرآن، وتعجبوا منه أن يسقطوا على النبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the jinn piled upon one another out of desire for what they had heard.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r7.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: يعني الجن كانوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r8.claim: Abu ʿUbayda defines libadan as crowds; its singular is libda, also used for a great mass of locusts.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r9.speaker: عبد مناف بن ربع الهذلي وأبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r9.claim: The poem describes locusts as a packed mass, and Abu ʿUbayda explains al-jābī as locusts because they gather what they eat.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r10.claim: Abu Ishaq says it means piling one thing tightly on another; labad are felt mats, from the same root.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r11.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r11.claim: Al-Farra gives the same explanation for labad and lubad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r11.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الفراء في اللبد، واللبد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r12.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r12.claim: Al-Kisaʾi glosses it as piled-up heaps, the plural of libda.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r12.anchor: وقال الكسائي: لبدا: ركاما، جمع لبدة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r13.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r13.claim: Abu ʿAli al-Farisi says lubad with ḍamma means a great many, as in “I have spent abundant wealth”; here it suggests their closeness while listening, and the kasra reading is more familiar for this sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p318/r13.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: (اللبد -بضم اللام- الكثير من قوله: {أهلكت مالا لبدا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r1.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad says libad means crowds, singular libda, from things piled onto one another; a lion is called dhū libda for the matted hair between its shoulders.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r1.anchor: وقال المبرد: اللبد: الجماعات، واحدها: "لبدة"، وأصله ما وقع بعضه على بعض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r2.speaker: زهير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r2.claim: Zuhayr’s line about a lion with untrimmed claws is cited as evidence for the lion’s matted mane, labd.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r3.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad distinguishes labad meaning many from labad as a singular rather than a plural, like ḥaṭam for a man.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r3.anchor: وقال: "لبد" كثير، و"لبد" واحد ليس جمعا لشيء، كقوله: رجل حطم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports from Ibn Abbas that the jinn saw the Prophet and his companions praying and prostrating together and marvelled at the companions’ obedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r4.anchor: وهو قول سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: لما رأوه يصلي وأصحابه يصلون بصلاته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r5.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r5.claim: Qatada says that when the Prophet began preaching, humans and jinn massed against him to extinguish God’s light, but God resolved to support and make him prevail; al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd share this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p321/r5.anchor: قول قتادة، قال: لما قام عبد الله بالدعوة

QASHANI:72:18-21/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:72:18-21/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:72:18-21/r3.claim: God's servant is the heart turned toward truth, humble and obedient, calling by turning to Him, seeking His light, and glorifying Him.
QASHANI:72:18-21/r3.anchor: القلب المتوجه إلى الحق الخاشع المطيع

QASHANI:72:18-21/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:72:18-21/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:72:18-21/r4.claim: The faculties nearly crowd around the heart by gaining mastery and veiling it through their appearance and dominance.
QASHANI:72:18-21/r4.anchor: يزدحمون عليه بالاستيلاء ويحجبونه بالظهور والغلبة

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:19/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:19/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:19/r1.claim: “God’s servant” means the Prophet; God honored His messenger by associating him with His own exalted person.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:19/r1.anchor: “Allah’ın kulu”ndan maksat Hz. Peygamber’dir. Allah Teâlâ resulünü onurlandırmak için onu yüce zâtına izâfe ederek anmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:19/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:19/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:19/r2.claim: At Nakhlah, while Muhammad led his companions in prayer, the jinn surrounded him so closely to hear the Qur’an that they nearly trampled one another.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:19/r2.anchor: Âyette Hz. Peygamber Nahle denilen yerde ashabına namaz kıldırırken cinlerin ondan Kur’an dinlemek için neredeyse birbirlerini çiğneyecek şekilde etrafını kuşattıkları ifade edilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:19/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:19/r3.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:19/r3.claim: An alternative reading says jinn and humans supported one another to destroy the religion Muhammad brought when he began worshipping and calling to God; Tabari prefers this interpretation, though God gave them no opportunity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:72:19/r3.anchor: yok etmek için birbirlerini destekliyorlardı, ancak Allah onlara fırsat vermedi.” Taberî bu anlamı tercih etmiştir

BURHAN:v4p29/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p29/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p29/r8.claim: A separation pronoun may be first, second, or third person and has syntactic case; a pronoun of affair is third person only and nominative.
BURHAN:v4p29/r8.anchor: والفرق بينه وبين ضمير الفصل إن الفصل يكون على لفظ الغائب والمتكلم والمخاطب

BURHAN:v2p410/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p410/r3.speaker: جماعة من النحاة
BURHAN:v2p410/r3.claim: Many grammarians parse هو as a pronoun of affair, with الله as a second subject and أحد its predicate; the clause explains the pronoun and needs no antecedent.
BURHAN:v2p410/r3.anchor: قال جماعة من النحاة هو ضمير الشأن والله مبتدأ ثان وأحد خبر المبتدأ الثاني

BURHAN:v1p362/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p362/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p362/r1.claim: If أنه لما قام is opened, it may be a fourth clause; if the particle after سمعنا is opened, this and the following clauses through حطبا can instead be counted inside the reported speech.
BURHAN:v1p362/r1.anchor: رابعة تابعة فإن فتحت التى بعد ﴿ سمعنا ﴾ كانت هى واللواتى بعدها إلى قوله ﴿ حطبا ﴾

BURHAN:v1p362/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p362/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p362/r4.claim: A complete pause may allow a delay between utterances; an incomplete pause permits only a brief breath within one utterance, and the still weaker type allows no interval.
BURHAN:v1p362/r4.anchor: أن التام قد يجوز أن يقع فيه بين القولين مهلة وتراخ فى اللفظ والناقص لا يجوز أن يقع فيه بين جزأى القول إلا قليل لبث

BURHAN:v3p151/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p151/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p151/r1.claim: A poetic example uses masculine agreement for Barada's water; agreement with the overt feminine noun would instead use feminine tāʾ.
BURHAN:v3p151/r1.anchor: بالياء أي ماء بردى ولو راعى المذكور لأتى بالتاء

ITQAN:v1p129#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p129#3/r1.speaker: عائشة
ITQAN:v1p129#3/r1.claim: Aisha reports that revelation made the Prophet’s head droop, his face change color, his teeth feel cold, and sweat run like pearls.
ITQAN:v1p129#3/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن سعد عن عائشة قالت كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه الوحي يغط في رأسه ويتربد وجهه أي يتغير لونه

ITQAN:v1p129#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p129#3/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p129#3/r2.claim: The seven-aḥruf report comes from twenty-one Companions; Abu ʿUbayd explicitly considered it mutawātir.
ITQAN:v1p129#3/r2.anchor: قلت ورد حديث نزل القرآن على سبعة أحرف من رواية جمع من الصحابة أبي بن كعب وأنس وحذيفة بن اليمان وزيد بن أرقم

ITQAN:v1p129#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p129#3/r3.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
ITQAN:v1p129#3/r3.claim: A report from ʿUthmān says witnesses affirmed the Prophet’s statement that all seven aḥruf are sound and sufficient, and ʿUthmān joined their testimony.
ITQAN:v1p129#3/r3.anchor: وأخرج أبو يعلى في مسنده أن عثمان قال على المنبر أذكر الله رجلا سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن القرآن أنزل على سبعة أحرف كلها شاف كاف

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r1.claim: The cited lines picture distinguished men whose standing opens kings’ gates for them, while mere approach does not guarantee entry.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r1.anchor: ليس كل من دنا من أبواب الملوك فتحت له

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r2.claim: Verbal complexity is blameworthy when words are ordered so that the intended meaning is not clear and the listener must find it by an indirect route.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r2.anchor: وأما التعقيد فإنما كان مذموما لأجل أن اللفظ لم يرتب الترتيب الذي يمثله تحصل الدلالة على الغرض

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r3.claim: Effort can make discovery more pleasurable when the meaning merits it, but exhausting labor for a poor result has the opposite effect.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r3.anchor: فرحا بالمعنى وأنسا به وسرورا بالوقوف عليه إذا كان لذلك أهلا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r4.claim: The worst complexity tires without benefit and resembles a miser who keeps someone hoping with promises, then offers nothing worth the effort.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r4.anchor: أحق أصناف التعقيد بالذم ما يتعبك ثم لا يجدي عليك ويؤرقك ثم لا يروق لك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r5.claim: The author faults Abu Tammam for strained diction and constructions so obscure that grammar cannot readily repair them.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r5.anchor: مثل ما تجده لأبى تمام من تعسفه في اللفظ وذهابه به في نحو من التركيب لا يهتدى النحو إلى إصلاحه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r6.claim: Abu Tammam’s line about a ‘second’ in the middle of the sky and two men having no second in the cave exemplifies this contrived arrangement.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p120/r6.anchor: يعمي الإعراب في طريقه ويصل في تعريفه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r1.claim: Qiyām is the human body’s upright posture; qawma is one standing, qiwām what something depends on, and qiwām can mean good stature.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r1.anchor: الأصل في القيام : انه انتصاب القامة من الآدمي وامتدادها إلى جهة العلو

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r7.claim: Qāma can mean rising to undertake a call or mission.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r7.anchor: السادس : النهوض بالدعوة . ومنه قوله تعالى في المدثر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r8.claim: Qiyām can mean coming to be or occurring, as in the Hour arising.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p504/r8.anchor: السابع : الكون . ومنه قوله تعالى في مواضع

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#3/r1.claim: “God’s servant” is the Prophet, who stood calling people to God.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#3/r1.anchor: أي لما قام النبي-صلى الله عليه وسلم- يدعو إليه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#3/r2.claim: They nearly clustered and piled around him, eager for the Qur’an and keen to hear it; libad is the plural of libda, a clump that sticks together.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#3/r2.anchor: {كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} أي يلبدون به [ويتراكبون] : (6) رغبة في القرآن، وشهوة لاستماعه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#3/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#3/r3.claim: He cites the usage “a clump of illicit gain covered him” to illustrate something accumulated and clinging to a person.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p491#3/r3.anchor: يقال: غشيته لبدة من الحرام (7) أي قطعة لبدت به.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r12.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r12.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r12.claim: Annahu is accusative and coordinated with earlier clauses; the phrase means when the Prophet stood calling upon God.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r12.anchor: وأنه لما قام عبد الله [الجن: 19] بنصب (أن) نسق على ما تقدم من قوله سبحانه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r13.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r13.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r13.claim: The jinn nearly crowded and piled over one another around him, eager for what they heard and desiring it.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p243/r13.anchor: يعني الجن كادوا يلبدون به ويتراكبون، رغبة فيما سمعوا منه، وشهوة له

NAHHAS:v5p50/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p50/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p50/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses لِبَدا as helpers.
NAHHAS:v5p50/r13.anchor: روى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس لبدا أعوانا

NAHHAS:v5p50/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p50/r14.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v5p50/r14.claim: Mujāhid glosses it as gathered groups, or abundant wealth; the author calls the explanation clear and favors the crowd sense over mere abundance.
NAHHAS:v5p50/r14.anchor: لبدا جماعات ومالا لبدا كثيرا قال أبو جعفر وهذا قول بين

NAHHAS:v5p50/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p50/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p50/r15.claim: The root image is things accumulating and sticking together; لبدة can be a mass of hair or similar material.
NAHHAS:v5p50/r15.anchor: من تلبد الشيء على الشيء إذا تجمع عليه ولصق به وعليه لبدة أي شعر

SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r1.claim: يدعوه is circumstantial, meaning that the servant was invoking God as a monotheist.
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r1.anchor: قوله: { يدعوه }: في موضع الحال أي: داعيا، أي: موحدا له

SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r2.speaker: هشام
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r2.claim: Hishām reads لبدا with ḍamma on lām; remaining readers use kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r2.anchor: قرأ هشام بضم اللام، والباقون بكسرها

SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r3.claim: With ḍamma on lām, لبدا may be plural of لبدة or a singular descriptive adjective like حطم; the latter use occurs at 90:6.
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r3.anchor: جمع لبدة بضم اللام نحو: غرفة وغرف. وقيل: بل هو اسم مفرد صفة

SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r4.claim: With kasra, لبدا is plural of لبدة, describing something piled and matted together like a lion's mane.

SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r5.claim: A poetic line about a mane whose claws have not been clipped witnesses the piled-mane sense of لبدة.

SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r6.claim: لبد is also the name of Luqmān ibn ʿĀd's eagle; the jinn nearly formed a densely packed crowd around the Prophet.
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r6.anchor: ومنه " اللبد " لتلبد بعضه فوق بعض، ولبد: اسم نسر لقمان ابن عاد

SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r7.speaker: الحسن والجحدري
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Jaḥdarī read لبدا with two ḍammas, possibly a plural of لبد or لبود, on patterns رهن/رهن and صبور/صبر.
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والجحدري " لبدا " بضمتين، ورواها جماعة عن أبي عمرو، وهي تحتمل وجهين

SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r8.speaker: ابن محيصن
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r8.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin reads with ḍamma and quiescent b; it may reduce the preceding reading or be an independent adjective.
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن بضمة وسكون، فيجوز أن تكون هذه مخففة من القراءة التي قبلها

SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r9.speaker: الحسن والجحدري
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Jaḥdarī also read doubled b with ḍamma on lām, as a plural of لابد like ساجد/سجد.
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r9.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والجحدري أيضا " لبدا " بضم اللام وتشديد الباء، وهو جمع " لابد "

SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r10.speaker: أبو رجاء
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r10.claim: Abū Rajāʾ reads with kasra on lām and doubled b, a reading called highly unusual.
SAMIN-DURR:72:19/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء بكسر/ اللام وتشديد الباء وهي غريبة جدا

ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r1.claim: The word lubadan has more than one reading, with the source distinguishing vocalized forms that are represented alike in its unvowelled text.

ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r2.claim: One explanation takes the subject as the jinn: after hearing and marveling at the Qur'an during the Prophet's dawn prayer at Dhāt Nakhlah, they nearly fell upon him.
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r2.anchor: والمعنى أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لما صلى الصبح بذات نخلة

ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r3.claim: Another explanation takes the subject as the opposing host who had banded together against the Prophet.
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r3.anchor: وقيل كادوا يعني به جميع الملأ التي تظاهرت على النبي

ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r4.claim: Lubad describes things piled tightly on one another; the root also gives the name of the densely felted rugs.
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r4.anchor: ومعنى (لبدا) يركب بعضه بعضا، وكل شيء ألصقته بشيء

ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r5.claim: One reading is parsed as a plural of libda or libd; another is treated as a plural of forms such as libda and libda, which the source says share a sense.
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r5.anchor: فأما من قرأ لبدا فهو جمع لبدة ولبد. ومن قرأ

ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r6.claim: A further analysis makes lubad a plural of lābid, on the pattern of rākiʿ to rakaʿ and ghāzin to ghuzā.
ZAJJAJ:v5p236#2/r6.anchor: ومعنى من قرأ (لبدا) فهو جمع لابد ولبد، مثل راكع وركع

ASAD-NOTES:72:18/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:18/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:72:18/r2.claim: Whenever God's servant stands in prayer, truth-deniers gather around and try to overwhelm him.
ASAD-NOTES:72:18/r2.anchor: whenever a servant of God stands up in prayer to Him

ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r1.claim: Libad, singular libdah, means that the crowds would almost be upon the servant.
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r1.anchor: upon him in crowds (libad, sing. libdah

ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r2.speaker: Tabari
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r2.claim: Tabari reads the crowding as an attempt to extinguish God's guiding light, alluding to 9:32.

ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r3.speaker: Most commentators
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r3.claim: Most commentators take the initial reference to be Muhammad and the hostility of his pagan contemporaries.
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r3.anchor: Most of the commentators assume that the above verse refers to the Prophet Muhammad and the hostility shown to him by his pagan contemporaries

ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r4.claim: Asad allows that initial setting but emphasizes a general pattern: majorities in every society oppose an individual or minority defending an evident but unpopular moral truth.
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r4.anchor: the passage has a general import as well, alluding to the hostility shown by the majority of people, at all times and in all societies

ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r5.claim: Asad says the verse should be read with 19:73–74 and its notes.
ASAD-NOTES:72:18#n15/r5.anchor: read in conjunction with 19:73-74 and the corresponding notes

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r11.claim: Chosen servitude means devoting oneself to God's worship and pleasure; people rank according to its completeness, and the term honors prophets.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#8/r11.anchor: العبودية الاختيارية وهي أن يجعل الشخص نفسه عبداً خالصاً لله موطّناً نفسه على عبادته متحرياً مرضاته ساعياً في طاعته

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr open the hamza in four clauses; Nafi and Abu Bakr's Asim transmission agree except they kasra وإنه لما at 72:19, while Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisai open all except after speech or a jawab فاء; Hafs matches Hamza.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p330/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو: قل أوحي إلي أنه [1]، وأن لو استقاموا [16] وأن المساجد لله [18]، وأنه لما قام عبد الله [19] أربعة أحرف بالفتح

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333#2/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333#2/r1.claim: The قال reading continues the preceding third-person narration; the imperative قل fits the repeated second-person commands in verses 21–22.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p333#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو علي: وجه من قال أن ذكر الغيبة قد تقدم، وهو قوله:

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r1.claim: These four instances of an vary between fatḥa, coordinated with “it was revealed to me,” and kasra, coordinated with “they said: we heard”; after fa in a conditional response, kasra alone is used.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p354/r1.anchor: هذه الأربعة تقرأ بالفتح وباقي ما قبلها بالكسر فالفتح بالعطف

IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr open the hamza in all four cited clauses.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ﴿ قل أوحي إلي أنه استمع ﴾ ﴿ وأن لو استقاموا على الطريقة ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r2.speaker: عاصم فى رواية أبى بكر ونافع، والمفضل عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r2.claim: Abu Bakr's transmission from Asim and Nafi match Abu Amr except that both read the hamza in وأنه لما قام عبد الله with kasra; al-Mufaddal transmits the same from Asim.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم فى رواية أبى بكر ونافع كما قرأ أبو عمرو

IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائى وحفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r3.claim: These readers open the hamza except where the clause follows a statement or a fāʾ of recompense.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p656/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائى وحفص عن عاصم كل ذلك بالفتح إلا ما جاء بعد قول أو بعد فاء جزاء

NASHR:v2p391#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p391#2/r7.speaker: نافع، وأبو بكر
NASHR:v2p391#2/r7.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr read the hamza of wa-annahu lammā qāma with kasra; the remaining readers use fatḥa.
NASHR:v2p391#2/r7.anchor: وأنه لما قام فقرأ نافع، وأبو بكر بكسر الهمزة، وقرأ الباقون بفتحها

NASHR:v2p391#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p391#2/r8.speaker: هشام
NASHR:v2p391#2/r8.claim: Hishām has a damma-on-lām reading through Ibn ʿAbdān from al-Ḥalwānī, and a kasra-on-lām reading through al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān; both are sound and the author read both.
NASHR:v2p391#2/r8.anchor: فروى هشام من طريق ابن عبدان عن الحلواني بضم اللام

NASHR:v2p391#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p391#2/r9.speaker: الفضل بن شاذان
NASHR:v2p391#2/r9.claim: Al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān reports kasra on the lām from al-Ḥalwānī; both lām vowels are sound from Hishām, while the other readers use kasra.
NASHR:v2p391#2/r9.anchor: ورواه بكسر اللام الفضل بن شاذان عن الحلواني

NASHR:v1p21/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
NASHR:v1p21/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's wording says not to abandon one of the revealed forms for another out of disdain.
NASHR:v1p21/r1.anchor: وفي لفظ لابن مسعود: " فمن قرأ على حرف منها فلا يتحول إلى غيره رغبة عنه "

NASHR:v1p21/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21/r2.speaker: أبو بكرة
NASHR:v1p21/r2.claim: Abū Bakra's wording says each form is sufficient, provided a verse of punishment is not ended with mercy or a verse of mercy with punishment.
NASHR:v1p21/r2.anchor: وفي لفظ لأبي بكرة: " كل شاف كاف ما لم تختم آية عذاب برحمة وآية رحمة بعذاب "

NASHR:v1p21/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21/r3.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
NASHR:v1p21/r3.claim: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ's wording says whichever form people recite is correct and forbids disputing over it, calling such disputation unbelief.
NASHR:v1p21/r3.anchor: وفي لفظ لعمرو بن العاص: " فأي ذلك قرأتم فقد أصبتم ولا تماروا فيه، فإن المراء فيه كفر "

NASHR:v1p21/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام
NASHR:v1p21/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayd states that the seven-letters hadith is mutawātir; the author says he traced it through nineteen Companions.
NASHR:v1p21/r4.anchor: الإمام الكبير أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام - رحمه الله - على أن هذا الحديث تواتر عن النبي

NASHR:v1p21/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21/r5.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
NASHR:v1p21/r5.claim: A report from ʿUthmān says many people witnessed the Prophet state that the Quran was revealed in seven sufficient forms, and ʿUthmān joined their testimony.
NASHR:v1p21/r5.anchor: أنزل القرآن على سبعة أحرف كلها شاف كاف فقال عثمان

NASHR:v1p21/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p21/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p21/r6.claim: The author organizes discussion of the seven-letters hadith into ten questions, beginning with its occasion, meaning, intended sense, why seven, and how the variation maps to seven.
NASHR:v1p21/r6.anchor: أن الكلام عليه ينحصر في عشرة أوجه: (الأول) في سبب وروده. (الثاني) في معنى الأحرف

QIRAAT-ER:72:19:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:72:19:2#1/r1.speaker: in↔an
QIRAAT-ER:72:19:2#1/r1.claim: Kasra gives wa-innahu as an independent emphatic assertion; fatḥa gives wa-annahu as subordinate to the governing verb.
QIRAAT-ER:72:19:2#1/r1.anchor: in↔an, mutawatir: Kasra on hamza: inna (emphatic/assertive) vs anna (subordinating)

QIRAAT-ER:72:19:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:72:19:11#1/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:72:19:11#1/r1.claim: With ḍamma on lām, lubadan is a plural of lubdah, a compact group, emphasizing several distinct clusters rather than one undifferentiated mass.
QIRAAT-ER:72:19:11#1/r1.anchor: vw, mutawatir: Ḍamma on lām: lubadan — plural of lubdah (a single compact group)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323#2/r1.claim: Qatāda explains “libadan” as the jinn and humans crowding together after the Prophet was sent, intent on extinguishing the light revealed to him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ لبدا ﴾ قال لما بعث الله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تلبدت الجن والإنس

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323#2/r2.speaker: الزبير
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323#2/r2.claim: Al-Zubayr places this event at Nakhlah, while the Prophet was reciting during the evening prayer.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p323#2/r2.anchor: قال الزبير كان ذلك بنخلة والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ في العشاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p291/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p291/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p291/r12.claim: Libad is a mass piled layer upon layer, as a lion’s mane or dense locust swarm; it can also name a felted wool mat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p291/r12.anchor: اللبد، جمع لبدة: وهو تراكم بعضه فوق بعض، ومنه لبدة الأسد.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r1.claim: The majority read the hamza of “annahu” with fatḥa, coordinating the clause with “He listened”; it remains part of the divine revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r1.anchor: وأنه بفتح الهمزة عند الجمهور على أنه عطف على أنه استمع كالذي قبله فهو من كلامه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r2.claim: “God’s servant” is the Prophet, who rose to pray the dawn prayer at Nakhlah.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r2.anchor: أي النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r3.claim: “Calling upon Him” is a circumstantial clause describing God’s servant as he rose in worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى يدعوه حال من عبد أي لما قام عابدا له عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk take “they” as the jinn, who nearly crowded over the Prophet in amazement at his worship, recitation, and the companions’ prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r4.anchor: كادوا أي الجن كما قال ابن عباس والضحاك يكونون عليه لبدا متراكمين من ازدحامهم عليه تعجبا مما شاهدوا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r5.claim: Their crowding reflects their astonishment at worship and recitation unlike anything they had seen or heard; the scene suggests a large jinn audience, not merely nine or so.
