ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r5.anchor: لأنهم رأوا ما لم يروا مثله وسمعوا ما لم يسمعوا نظيره وهذا كالظاهر في أنهم كانوا كثيرين لا تسعة ونحوها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r6.claim: Calling him “the servant” suits a report spoken in obedience to the revelation and highlights the humility of servanthood; alternatively, God chose the title to show that worship by a servant is unsurprising.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r6.anchor: إما لأنه مقول على لسانه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لأنه أمر يقول أوحي كذا فجيء به على ما يقتضيه مقام العبودية والتواضع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r7.claim: A further explanation is that the Prophet transmits God’s wording as it is, removing himself from the account so that no trace of personal intervention remains.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r7.anchor: ونقل عليه الصلاة والسلام كلامه سبحانه كما هو رفعا لنفسه عن البين فلا وجود للأثر بعد العين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r8.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda take “they” as Quraysh and the Arabs: the Prophet’s rise is his mission, and their piling around him is their united hostility.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة ضمير كادوا لكفار قريش والعرب فيراد بالقيام القيام بالرسالة وبالتلبد للعداوة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r9.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r9.claim: Qatāda also reports that jinn and humans massed against the message to extinguish it, but God would support the Prophet against opponents.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r9.anchor: وعن قتادة أيضا ما يقتضيه قال تلبدت الإنس والجن على هذا الأمر ليطفؤه فأبى الله تعالى إلا أن ينصره

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r10.claim: On the hostile-crowd interpretation, another possibility is that the pronoun denotes both jinn and humans.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r10.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الضمير على هذا للجن والإنس

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r11.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan’s report that the servant was Noah, nearly killed by his people before God rescued him, is remote; the identification with ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām is even less credible.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r11.anchor: حتى ايتنقذه الله تعالى منهم قاله الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r12.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر وابن هرمز وطلحة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r12.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū Bakr, Ibn Hurmuz, and Ṭalḥa read “annahu” with kasra, as an independent sentence; it may begin God’s statement or continue the jinn’s report.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r12.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو بكر كما قدمنا وابن هرمز وطلحة كما في البحر وأنه بكسر الهمزة وحمل على أن الجملة استئنافية

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r13.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r13.claim: Ibn Jubayr’s reading of the verse as the jinn reporting what they witnessed keeps the account continuous with their return to their people.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r13.anchor: وجوز أن تكون من كلام الجن معطوفة على جملة إنا سمعنا حكموا فيها لقومهم لما رجعوا إليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r14.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r14.claim: Al-Kashf prefers continuity: if the mosques clause belongs to the revelation, the prohibition addresses the jinn, and the kasra reading continues their report, avoiding a break in the narrative.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r14.anchor: وفي الكشف الوجه على تقدير أن يكون وإن المساجد من جملة الموحى أن يكون فلا تدعوا خطابا للجن محكيا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r15.claim: If the address is general, “they” can be the polytheists or both jinn and humans, while the kasra reading begins a fresh divine account that reinforces the preceding lesson.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r15.anchor: وأما لو جعل خطابا عاما فالوجه أن يكون ضمير كادوا راجعا إلى المشركين أو إلى الجن والإنس

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r16.claim: The contrast pairs the command that all worship God alone with the crowd’s hostility to the one who worships Him, a deliberate and elegant transition.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r16.anchor: وما أحسن التقابل بين قوله تعالى وإن المساجد وبين هذا القول كأنهم نهوا كلهم عن الإشراك ودعوا إلى التوحيد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r17.claim: If “mosques” means the seven bodily prostration points, verses 21–22 recall them as gifts made to serve God, clarifying the connection and the incompatibility of associating partners.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r17.anchor: والآيتان 21 و 22 على هذا على الأعضاء السبعة أظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r18.claim: “Libad” means piled-up groups, like layers pressed over one another; the word is also used of locusts, as illustrated by ʿAbd Manāf’s verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p92/r18.anchor: ويقال للجراد ومنه كما قال الجبائي قول عبد مناف بن ربع الهذلي صافوا بستة أبيات وأربعة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r1.claim: The verse continues the image of the crowd as a piled mass.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r2.speaker: مجاهد وابن محيصن وابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r2.claim: Mujāhid, Ibn Muḥayṣin, and Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission read with ḍamma on the lām, as a plural of libdah; Ibn Muḥayṣin also has a variant with a still bāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r2.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وابن محيصن وابن عامر بخلاف عنه لبدا بضم اللام جمع لبدة كزبرة وزبر وعن ابن محيصن أيضا تسكين الباء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r3.speaker: الحسن والجحدري وأبو حيوة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Jaḥdarī, Abū Ḥaywah, and a group transmitting from Abū ʿAmr read with ḍamma on both consonants, either as the plural of libd or of lubūd.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والجحدري وأبو حيوة وجماعة عن أبي عمرو بضمتين جمع لبد كرهن ورهن أو جمع لبود كصبور وصبر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r4.speaker: الحسن والجحدري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Jaḥdarī also have a variant with a doubled bāʾ, treated as the plural of lābid.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والجحدري أيضا بخلاف عنهما لبدا بضم اللام وتشديد الباء جمع لا بد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r5.speaker: أبو رجاء
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r5.claim: Abū Rajāʾ reads the word with kasra on the lām and a doubled, open bāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p93/r5.anchor: وأبو رجاء بكسرها وشد الباء المفتوحة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r9.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r9.claim: Nafi and Abu Bakr read the hamza in wa-annahu with kasra; the other readers use fatḥa.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r9.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو بكر بكسر الهمزة، وقرأ الباقون بفتحها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r10.claim: Abd Allah refers to the Prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r10.anchor: يعني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r11.claim: He was worshipping God and reciting the Quran while praying at Batn Nakhlah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r11.anchor: يدعوه} يعني يعبده ويقرأ القرآن، ذلك حين كان يصلي ببطن نخلة ويقرأ القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r12.speaker: الضحاك ورواية عطية عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak and a report from Ibn Abbas through Atiyya say the jinn crowded on top of one another, eager to hear the Quran.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r12.anchor: هذا قول الضحاك ورواية عطية عن ابن عباس.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r13.claim: Libadan means crowding or piling closely on top of one another.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p242/r13.anchor: {يكونون عليه لبدا} أي يركب بعضهم بعضا ويزدحمون حرصا على استماع القرآن

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r1.claim: The “servant of God” is the Prophet; calling him servant is humble self-reference and points to the quality that occasioned his standing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r1.anchor: أي النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام وإنما ذكر بلفظ العبد للتواضع

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r2.claim: To call upon God here means to worship Him.

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r3.claim: The jinn nearly crowded around the Prophet, amazed at his worship and what they heard of his recitation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r3.anchor: كاد الجن. { يكونون عليه لبدا } متراكمين من ازدحامهم عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r4.claim: Alternatively, humans and jinn nearly gathered against him to frustrate his mission.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r4.anchor: أو كاد الإنس والجن يكونون عليه مجتمعين لإبطال أمره

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r5.claim: Labad is a pile, like the matted mane of a lion.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r5.anchor: وهو جمع لبدة وهي ما تلبد بعضه على بعض كلبدة الأسد

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r6.speaker: ابن عامر
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads lubadan with ḍamma on the lām, a dialectal plural of lubda.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عامر «لبدا» بضم اللام جمع لبدة وهي لغة

BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r7.claim: Other readings are lubadan, a plural of lābid, and lubadan like ṣubaran, a plural of labūd.
BAYDAWI-FULL:72:19-20/r7.anchor: وقرىء «لبدا» كسجدا جمع لابد و «لبدا» كصبر جمع لبود

DURR-FULL:v8p306/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r13.claim: Ibn Masud says that before the Hijra the Prophet drew a line for him, told him to wait and not be alarmed; black men resembling the Zutt then gathered around the Prophet, as the verse says.
DURR-FULL:v8p306/r13.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل الهجرة إلى نواحي مكة فخط لي خطا

DURR-FULL:v8p307/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والزبير بن العوام
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the jinn nearly climbed over the Prophet in eagerness when they heard his recitation, drawing close unseen until Gabriel came and taught him the revelation; al-Zubayr reports the same.
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} قال: لما سمعوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يتلوا القرآن كادوا يركبونه من الحرص

DURR-FULL:v8p307/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r2.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report says the jinn approached while the Prophet prayed with his companions, bowing and prostrating with him; amazed at their obedience, they told their people the verse’s words.
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} قال: لما أتى الجن على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي بأصحابه يركعون بركوعه ويسجدون بسجوده

DURR-FULL:v8p307/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas understands yadʿuhu here to mean calling people to him.
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه} أي يدعو إليه

DURR-FULL:v8p307/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r4.claim: Qatada says humans and jinn massed against the Prophet’s cause to extinguish it, but God insisted on supporting him and giving him victory over opponents.
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وإنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا}

DURR-FULL:v8p307/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says when the Messenger proclaimed there is no god but God and called people to their Lord, nearly all the Arabs massed against him.
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r5.anchor: عن الحسن {وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه} قال: لما قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: لا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v8p307/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses lubadan as supporters or helpers.
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} قال: أعوانا

DURR-FULL:v8p307/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r7.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r7.claim: Asim reads lubadan with kasra on the lām here, while in 90:6 he reads lubadan with ḍamma; Abu Bakr explains the forms as much and piled upon one another.
DURR-FULL:v8p307/r7.anchor: من طريق أبي بكر عن أبي عاصم أنه قرأ {يكونون عليه لبدا} بكسر اللام ونصب الباء

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3378#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3378#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3378#4/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “libadan” as helpers or supporters.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3378#4/r1.anchor: عن علي عن ابن عباس في قوله : كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا قال : اعوانا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r1.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr’s transmission from ʿĀṣim read the hamza in inna with kasra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وحده وأبو بكر عن عاصم بكسر الهمزة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r2.speaker: بقية العشرة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r2.claim: The remaining readers in their well-known transmissions read the hamza with fatḥa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r2.anchor: وقرأه بقية العشرة في رواياتهم المشهورة بالفتح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r3.claim: Both readings place the statement outside the jinn’s quotation and make it part of God’s revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r3.anchor: ومآل القراءتين سواء في كون هذا خارجا عما صدر عن الجن وفي كونه مما أوحى الله به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r4.claim: With kasra, the sentence coordinates with “it was revealed to me”; it means “say that when God’s servant stood calling Him,” since inna in quoted speech is kasra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r4.anchor: فكسر الهمزة على عطف الجملة على جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r5.claim: It cannot be treated as the jinn’s continuing speech: their report had ended and the passage had moved to other subjects beginning at 72:18.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r5.anchor: ولا يليق أن يجعل من حكاية مقالة الجن لأن ذلك قد انقضى وتباعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r6.claim: With fatḥa, the clause coordinates with the revelation that the jinn listened; God revealed that the polytheists nearly crowded around His servant as he prayed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r6.anchor: وأما الفتح فعلى اعتباره معطوفا على جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r7.claim: The pronoun in inna is a pronoun of the affair, with the clause beginning “when God’s servant stood” as its predicate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r7.anchor: وضمير { إنه } ضمير الشأن وجملة { لما قام عبد الله }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r8.claim: The pronouns “they” refer to the polytheists, who are suggested by the context from 72:16 through the prohibition in 72:18.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r8.anchor: وضمير { كادوا يكونون } عائدان إلى المشركين المنبىء عنهم المقام غيبة وخطابا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r9.claim: “God’s servant” is Muhammad; the explicit title replaces an expected pronoun to honor him through the ennobling association of servitude to God, as in 17:1.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p241/r9.anchor: و { عبد الله } هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وضع الاسم الظاهر موضع المضمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r1.claim: Lubadan is a collective noun for a mass whose parts are felted together, like the thick mane of a lion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r1.anchor: { ولبدا } بكسر اللام وفتح الموحدة اسم جمع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r2.claim: The polytheists nearly crowded tightly around Muhammad to hear his recitation and call to monotheism, gathering in anger and intent on harm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r2.anchor: كاد المشركون يكونون مثل اللبد متراصين مقتربين منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r3.claim: Qāma can mean striving in the call to God, as in the youths who stood and declared their faith in 18:14.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r3.anchor: اجتهد في الدعوة إلى الله ، كقوله تعالى :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r4.speaker: النابغة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r4.claim: Al-Nābighah’s line about the sons of Asad standing and proclaiming their protection illustrates qāma as taking a public stand and speaking.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r4.anchor: وقال النابغة : بأن حصنا وحيا من بني أسد قاموا فقالوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r5.speaker: جزء بن كليب الفقعسي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r5.claim: The line by Juzʾ ibn Kulayb al-Faqʿasī uses the Prophet’s rising as the start of his public worship of God alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r5.anchor: قال جزء بن كليب الفقعسي : فلا تبغينها يا بن كوز فإنه غذا الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r6.claim: The declaration “I only call upon my Lord” explains what the preceding clause means by the Prophet calling upon God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p242/r6.anchor: وجملة { قل إنما أدعو ربي ولا أشرك به أحدا } بيان لجملة { يدعوه }

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r8.speaker: ابن كثير، أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r8.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi reports that Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr open four hamzas in the surah and kasra-read the others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r8.anchor: وذكر أبو علي الفارسي أن ابن كثير وأبا عمرو فتحا أربعة أحرف من السورة وكسرا غير ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r9.speaker: نافع، عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r9.claim: Nafi and Asim in the Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal transmissions agree on three openings but kasra-read the clause at 72:19 and the rest.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r9.anchor: وأن نافعا وعاصما في رواية أبي بكر والمفضل وافقا في الثلاثة وكسرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r10.speaker: ابن عامر، حمزة، الكسائي، حفص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r10.claim: These readers open the surah's hamzas except after a saying or a consequential fa; this yields consensus on openings at 72:1, 72:16, and 72:18.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p378#2/r10.anchor: وذكر أن ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي كانوا يقرأون كل ما في السورة بالفتح إلا ما جاء بعد قول أو فاء جزاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r8.claim: The clause may be God's address or a report by the jinn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r8.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: وأنه لما قام عبد الله يحتمل أن يكون خطابا من الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r9.claim: With the opening reading, 72:19 is coordinated with 72:1; some identify the servant as Noah and those nearly crowding him as his disbelieving people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r9.anchor: وقرأ بعض القراء على ما تقدم «وأنه» بفتح الألف، وهذا عطف على قوله أنه استمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r10.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r10.claim: Some interpreters identify the servant as Noah and those nearly crowding him as his disbelieving people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r10.anchor: والعبد على هذه القراءة قال قوم: هو نوح، والضمير في كادوا لكفار قومه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r11.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r11.claim: Others identify the servant as Muhammad and those nearly pressing upon him as jinn straining to hear the Quran.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r11.anchor: وقال آخرون، هو محمد، والضمير في كادوا للجن. المعنى أنهم كادوا يتقصفون عليه لاستماع القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r12.claim: With kasra, the servant is Muhammad; those nearly crowding him may be jinn as above or disbelievers among his people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r12.anchor: وقرأ آخرون منهم «وإنه لما قام» بكسر الألف، والعبد محمد عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r13.claim: On the kasra reading, the pronoun can refer to jinn or to the servant's disbelieving people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p383/r13.anchor: والضمير في كادوا يحتمل أن يكون للجن على المعنى الذي ذكرناه، ويحتمل أن يكون لكفار قومه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r1.claim: ʿAbd Allāh refers to Muḥammad, who was worshipping God and praying in the valley of Nakhlah, as noted at 46:29.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r1.anchor: وأنه لما قام عبد الله يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم يدعوه أي يعبده وكان يصلي ببطن نخلة على ما سبق بيانه في الأحقاف 29

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r2.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r2.claim: The majority read libadan with kasra on lām and fatḥa on bāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r2.anchor: قرأ الأكثرون لبدا بكسر اللام وفتح الباء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r3.speaker: هشام عن ابن عامر، ابن محيصن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r3.claim: They read lubadan with ḍamma on lām and a light bāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r3.anchor: وقرأ هشام عن ابن عامر وابن محيصن لبدا بضم اللام وفتح الباء مع تخفيفها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r4.speaker: الحسن، الجحدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r4.claim: They read lubbadan with ḍamma on lām and a doubled bāʾ; on this reading it describes the men.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r4.anchor: وقرأ قوم منهم الحسن والجحدري لبدا بضم اللام مع تشديد الباء قال الفراء فعلى هذه القراءة يكون صفة للرجال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r5.claim: The two lighter readings have the same sense; people crowded on top of one another, like a felt mat, and anything piled onto something else is said to be labadtahu.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r5.anchor: قال الفراء ومعنى القراءتين واحد يقال لبدة ولبدة قال الزجاج والمعنى كاد يركب بعضهم بعضا ومنه اشتقاق اللبد الذي يفترش وكل شيء أضفته إلى شيء فقد لدبته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r6.claim: On the doubled reading, lubbadan is a plural of lābid, like rākiʿ and rukkaʿ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج هو جمع لابد مثل راكع وركع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r7.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r7.claim: One view says God describes the jinn crowding around the Prophet as he prayed, piling over one another in eagerness to hear the Qurʾān.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r7.anchor: أحدها أنه إخبار الله تعالى عن الجن يحكي حالهم والمعنى أنه لما قام يصلي كاد الجن لازدحامهم عليه يركب بعضهم بعضا حرصا على سماع القرآن رواه عطية عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r8.speaker: ابن جبير عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r8.claim: Another view has the jinn telling their people how Muhammad's followers obeyed and followed him in bowing and prostration.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r8.anchor: وهذا المعنى في رواية ابن جبير عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r9.speaker: الحسن، قتادة، ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r9.claim: A third view says humans and jinn united against the Messenger when he began preaching, trying to overcome the truth he brought.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p383/r9.anchor: والثالث أن المعنى لما قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالدعوة تلبدت الإنس والجن وتظاهروا عليه ليبطلوا الحق الذي جاء به قاله الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the jinn nearly crowded onto the Prophet from eagerness when they heard him reciting the Quran; they approached unseen until the angel informed him that jinn were listening. The cited revelation is 72:1.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r1.anchor: قال العوفي، عن ابن عباس يقول: لما سمعوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يتلو القرآن كادوا يركبونه؛ من الحرص، لما سمعوه يتلو القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r2.speaker: الزبير بن العوام
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir says the account of the jinn crowding near the Prophet to hear him is also transmitted from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r2.anchor: هذا قول، وهو مروي عن الزبير بن العوام، رضي الله عنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the jinn saw the Prophet and his companions praying, bowing and prostrating together, and marveled at the companions’ obedience to him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال الجن لقومهم: {وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies this second account of the jinn marveling at the companions’ prayerful obedience as also narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r4.anchor: وهذا قول ثان، وهو مروي عن سعيد بن جبير أيضا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the Arabs nearly massed against the Prophet when he declared that there is no god but God and called people to their Lord.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: لما قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "لا إله إلا الله" ويدعو الناس إلى ربهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r6.claim: Qatada says humans and jinn massed to extinguish the Prophet’s mission, but God insisted on supporting, advancing, and making it prevail over its opponents.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: {وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا} قال: تلبدت الإنس والجن على هذا الأمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir says this third interpretation is also attributed to Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and Ibn Zayd; it is al-Tabari’s choice and, in his view, the strongest reading.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p244#2/r7.anchor: هذا قول ثالث، وهو مروي عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير، وقول ابن زيد، واختيار ابن جرير، وهو الأظهر

JISHUMI:v10p7121/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7121/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7121/r4.claim: Libad means compacted layers like felted wool; labada can describe pressing hair together.
JISHUMI:v10p7121/r4.anchor: واللبد: القطع المتراكبة المتكاثفة، ومنه: اللبد لتراكب صوفه،

TIRMIDHI:3323/r2.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3323/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TIRMIDHI:3323/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the jinn's crowding around as amazement at the Prophet and companions praying together and following his prostrations; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
TIRMIDHI:3323/r2.anchor: عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ قَوْلُ الْجِنِّ لِقَوْمِهِمْ

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r10.claim: The servant of God who rises to call upon Him is Muhammad.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r10.anchor: وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه } يعني محمدا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muhammad stood in prayer calling on God while his companions followed him, and the jinn marveled at their obedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r11.anchor: أحدهما : أنه قام إلى الصلاة يدعو ربه فيها , وقام أصحابه خلفه مؤتمين , فعجبت الجن من طواعية أصحابه له , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r12.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r12.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Muhammad stood to call the Jews to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r12.anchor: الثاني : أنه قام إلى اليهود داعيا لهم إلى الله , رواه ابن جريج .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses libadan as helpers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r13.anchor: أحدهما : يعني أعوانا , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r14.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r14.claim: Mujahid glosses libadan as crowds piled one over another, like gathered wool.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r14.anchor: الثاني : جماعات بعضها فوق بعض , وهو معنى قول مجاهد , ومنه اللبد لاجتماع الصوف بعضه على بعض

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r15.speaker: ذو الرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r15.claim: Dhu al-Rumma is cited for a poetic witness to libadan's sense of a gathered mass.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p119/r15.anchor: ومنه اللبد لاجتماع الصوف بعضه على بعض , وقال ذو الرمة :

NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r1.claim: “God's servant” is Muhammad as he rose to pray; the construction implies “وأوحي إلي أنه لما قام”.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r1.anchor: محمدعليه السلام إلى الصلاة وتقديره وأوحى إلى أنه لما قام عبد الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r2.claim: He was worshipping God and reciting the Qur'an.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ يدعوه ﴾ يعبده ويقرأ القرآن ولم يقل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r3.claim: The wording “servant of God” is dear to the Prophet; it also suits humility in his own speech, or signals that his worship is no surprise warranting a crowd.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r3.anchor: لأنه من أحب الاسماء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولأنه لما كان واقعا في كلامه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r4.claim: The jinn nearly crowded around him in groups, marveling at his worship, imitating his companions, and admiring a recitation unlike anything they had seen.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p288#4/r4.anchor: تعجبا مما رأوا من عبادته واقتداء أصحابه به واعجابا بما تلاه من القرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that when the jinn saw the Prophet praying with his companions and they followed his prostration, they marveled at their obedience and said they nearly crowded around him.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:1-2/r6.anchor: رواه الترمذي عن ابن عباس قال

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r1.claim: The opening conjunction may be read with fatḥ as part of revelation to the Prophet, or with kasr as a new sentence.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r1.anchor: يجوز الفتح أي أوحى الله إليه أنه. ويجوز الكسر على الاستئناف

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r2.claim: Abd Allah is Muhammad, praying and reciting Quran at Batn Nakhlah, as recounted at the sura’s beginning.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r2.anchor: «عبد الله» هنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم حين كان يصلي ببطن نخلة

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r3.claim: The verb means that Muhammad worshipped God.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r3.anchor: أي يعبده. وقال ابن جريج: «يدعوه» أي قام إليهم داعيا

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj takes it to mean Muhammad stood calling the jinn to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r4.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: «يدعوه» أي قام إليهم داعيا إلى الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r5.speaker: الزبير بن العوام
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r5.claim: Al-Zubayr says the jinn nearly piled on one another when they heard the Prophet reciting, eager to listen.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r5.anchor: قال الزبير بن العوام: هم الجن حين استمعوا القرآن من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r6.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says they crowded one upon another out of eagerness to hear.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r6.anchor: وقيل: كادوا يركبونه حرصا قاله الضحاك

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the jinn crowded together because they wanted to hear the remembrance.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r7.anchor: ابن عباس: رغبة في سماع الذكر

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r8.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r8.claim: Burd reports from Makhul that seventy thousand jinn pledged allegiance to the Prophet that night and finished at daybreak; no grading is given.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r8.anchor: وروى برد عن مكحول: أن الجن بايعوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه الليلة

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r9.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas makes this the jinn’s account of Muhammad’s companions following him in bowing and prostration.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r9.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا: إن هذا من قول الجن لما رجعوا إلى قومهم

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r10.claim: Another view says the polytheists crowded against one another in hostility toward the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r10.anchor: وقيل: المعنى كاد المشركون يركبون بعضهم بعضا، حردا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r11.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r11.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd say humans and jinn massed against Muhammad at the valley to extinguish the light, but God granted victory and completed His light.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد: يعني { لما قام عبد الله } محمد بالعدوة تلبدت الإنس والجن

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r12.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r12.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that the Arabs nearly united against the Prophet to extinguish the light he brought.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r12.anchor: واختار الطبري أن يكون المعنى: كادت العرب يجتمعون على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r13.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r13.claim: Mujahid glosses lubad as crowds, from things piling together; the root also describes compacted wool or anything stuck tightly together.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r13.anchor: وقال مجاهد: قوله «لبدا» جماعات وهو من تلبد الشيء على الشيء أي تجمع

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r14.claim: The common reading has kasr on lam and fatḥ on ba; Mujahid, Ibn Muhaysin, and Hisham read damm on lam and fatḥ on ba, singular lubadah.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r14.anchor: وهي قراءة العامة. وضم اللام وفتح الباء، وهي قراءة مجاهد وابن محيصن وهشام عن أهل الشام

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r15.claim: Abu Haywah, Muhammad ibn al-Sumayqa, Abu al-Ashhab al-Uqayli, and al-Jahdari read damm on both letters; Hasan, Abu al-Aliyah, al-Araj, and al-Jahdari also read doubled ba with fatḥ.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r15.anchor: وبضم اللام والباء، وهي قراءة أبي حيوة ومحمد بن السميقع وأبي الأشهب العقيلي والجحدري

QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r16.claim: Another gloss takes lubad as enduring, as in Luqman’s last vulture, Lubad; al-Nabigha’s poetry evokes its survival.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:19/r16.anchor: وقيل: اللبد بضم اللام وفتح الباء الشيء الدائم ومنه قيل لنسر لقمان لبد

QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r1.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r1.claim: Al-Qushayri records lubadan with both letters rounded as plural of lubayd, a small sack.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r1.anchor: القشيري: وقرىء «لبدا» بضم اللام والباء، وهو جمع لبيد

QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r2.claim: Lubad in “I destroyed abundant wealth” means plentiful; people are also called lubad when assembled, while al-labad can mean a homebody.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r2.anchor: وفي الصحاح: وقوله تعالى أهلكت مالا لبدا [البلد: 6] أي جما

QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r3.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r3.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers a transmitted variant about a stay-at-home person; the cited verse praises good judgment and major undertakings.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r3.anchor: ويروى: اللبد. قال أبو عبيد: وهو أشبه. والبزلاء: الرأي الجيد

QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r4.claim: Arab lore says Luqman, sent by Ad to seek rain, chose seven vultures over seven ewes for long life; the last vulture was named Lubad.
QURTUBI-FULL:72:20-21/r4.anchor: وتزعم العرب أن لقمان هو الذي بعثته عاد في وفدها إلى الحرم يستسقي لها
